'''''Vertebrata fruticulosa'''''<ref name="Bunker">Bunker, F.StP., Bunker, D., Brodie, J.A., Maggs, C.A. and Bunker, A.R. 2017 ''Seaweeds of Britain and Ireland.''  Second Edition. Wild Nature Press, Plymouth, UK. {{ISBN|978-0-9955673-3-7}}</ref>(''Boergeseniella fruticulosa'' (Wulfen) Kylin)<ref name="Maggs">Maggs, C.A. and Hommersand, M.H. 1993.''Seaweeds of the British Isles of the British Isles Volume 1 Rhodophyta Part 3A Ceramiales'' The Natural History Museum, London. {{ISBN|0-11-310045-0}}</ref> is a small marine [[alga]] in the Division Rhodophyta.

==Description==
''Vertebrata fruticulosa'' is a small branched alga growing to 15 cm long. The erect axes are surrounded by 11 to 12 pericentral cells all of the same length. Cortication of small cells cover these branches. They are attached by [[rhizoids]].<ref name="Maggs"/>
Very similar to ''[[Vertebrata thuyoides]]'' and certain other species of ''Polysiphonia''.<ref name="Bunker"/><ref name="Maggs"/>

==Reproduction==
There are male and female plants. Spermatangial branches grow near the apices of the young branches. [[Cystocarp]]s are sessile. [[Tetraspore]]s are formed near the ends of the branches distorting it into a spiral shape.<ref name="Maggs"/>

==Habitat==
Epiphytic on other algae such as ''Corallina'' also on rock in rock pools in the littoral.<ref name="Maggs"/>

==Distribution==
In the eastern Atlantic from the Shetland Isles,<ref name="Bunker"/> Britain, Ireland, Morocco and the Mediterranean.<ref name="Maggs"/>
